candidate.answerReason: There are nine decreases of 7 between the first and tenth numbers, so the tenth number is 100−63=37.

methods.label: Count the steps from first to tenth
methods.explanation:
The starting number \(100\) is already the first number. Reaching the tenth number therefore takes \(10-1=9\) backward steps. Each step subtracts \(7\), so the total decrease is \(9\times7=63\). Thus the tenth number is
\[
100-9\times7=100-63=\boxed{37},
\]
choice \(\text{B}\).
